_doc: Wave 25 — follow_leader's own geometry (src/ai/actions/followLeader.ts).
Real world metres, chosen against real reference points the same way
combat.json's own _doc already does.
stopDistance 2.0 keeps Tam a companion's polite half-pace back rather
than jostling the player's own collision radius (PLAYER_RADIUS 0.45,
components/fps/PlayerController.tsx) — comfortably outside it, inside
conversational range.
runDistance 6 is the point a WALKING companion would otherwise visibly
fall behind a moving player — past it he switches to a run to close the
gap, the same walk/run split every other MOVE_TO issuer in this codebase
already makes. Verification fix (post-ship): the speeds this threshold
feeds into are COMPANION_WALK_SPEED (4.4) / COMPANION_RUN_SPEED (8.5),
ai/core/Locomotion.ts's own companion-only cap — NOT the villager-tuned
WALK_SPEED (0.9) / RUN_SPEED (1.6) this comment originally (and
wrongly) compared against each other. Those two never had the player's
own real speed (PlayerController.tsx's 4 m/s walk / 7 m/s sprint) in the
comparison at all, which is exactly how a companion who can only ever
hit 1.6 m/s shipped behind a player whose slowest gait is 4.
repathDistance 2.5 is engage_threat's own 1m re-aim margin (combat.json's
`engage` block has no named field for it — see engageThreat.ts's own
`Math.hypot(...) > 1` check), widened a little: the player moves far
more, and far more erratically (strafing, backing up, turning on a dime),
than a believed hostile's remembered position ever does, so a tighter
margin would re-issue an near-identical MOVE_TO (and re-stamp
Agent.intentSetAt) almost every think tick.
